;Armed conflicts and attacks
*[[Syrian Civil War]]
**The [[Israel Defense Forces|Israeli military]] [[Syria missile strikes (November 2019)|launches airstrikes]] on dozens of [[Quds Force]] targets in [[Damascus]] and surrounding towns in response to a missile intercepted the previous day over the [[Golan Heights]]. The [[Syrian Observatory for Human Rights]] reports 23 are killed, including several [[Iranian involvement in the Syrian Civil War|Iranian fighters]]. [https://apnews.com/ea7d21d0cbe24e899351b3ad56839fa2?fbclid=IwAR3EfZ-D5kgirXyhrD6Jiq392n6-LQHnRYjP4sNhkCSkJV5I2f0FbwuMBpQ (Associated Press)]
**Missiles and [[Airstrike|airstrikes]] strike a crowded facility in [[Qah]] and [[Idlib]], killing approximately over 20 including women and children. Activists claim that [[Syrian Armed Forces]] were behind the attack. [https://www.bbc.com/news/world-middle-east-50503857 (BBC News)]
*[[War in Afghanistan (2001–present)|War in Afghanistan]]
**The [[United States Armed Forces|U.S. military]] says two [[Americans|American]] service members have been killed in a helicopter crash in [[Afghanistan]]. [https://www.usatoday.com/story/news/world/2019/11/20/statement-says-wednesday-cause-crash-under-investigation-however-preliminary-reports-do-not-indicate/4246844002/?fbclid=IwAR0NlyMetzCk2PVAIspSxKD2_-1aZZxbgJElQgzeTSNBOXPI4CkBAN4ci2Q (''USA Today'')]
*[[2019 Bolivian protests]]
**The death toll in the protests rises to 30. [https://www.reuters.com/article/us-bolivia-politics/bolivian-lawmakers-seek-election-breakthrough-as-death-toll-hits-30-idUSKBN1XU1YJ (Reuters)]
*[[2019–2020 Iranian protests|2019 Iranian fuel protests]]
**According to the [[human rights]] organization [[Amnesty International]], casualties are estimated to be around 106 protestors and rising. [https://en.radiofarda.com/a/death-toll-in-iran-protests-rises-as-u-s-europe-condemn-use-of-force-/30280481.html (Radiofarda)]
*[[Yemeni Civil War (2015–present)]]
**[[Houthi movement|Houthi militants]] release the [[South Korea]]n ship they captured two days prior. [https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2019/11/yemen-houthis-release-captured-south-korean-saudi-vessels-191120080140333.html (Al Jazeera)]
*[[Allied Democratic Forces insurgency]]
**Militants target [[civilian]]s in the [[Democratic Republic of the Congo|DR Congo]] near the border with [[Uganda]], killing 19 and kidnapping others. Churches were also burned down in two separate attacks. It is believed that the [[Allied Democratic Forces]] is behind the attacks. [https://www.reuters.com/article/us-congo-security/suspected-islamist-militants-kill-19-burn-church-in-eastern-dr-congo-idUSKBN1XU2K6 (Reuters)]

;Arts and culture
*[[Prince Andrew, Duke of York]], halts all public duties in light of allegations of [[rape]], saying his "ill-judged" association with American convicted [[sex offender]] [[Jeffrey Epstein]] had caused major disruption to the [[British royal family|royal family]]'s work. [https://www.reuters.com/article/us-britain-royals-andrew-duties/britains-prince-andrew-halts-public-duties-over-sex-scandal-idUSKBN1XU2CW (Reuters)]

;Business and economy
*[[2019 Japan–South Korea trade dispute]]
**[[South Korea]]'s finance minister [[Hong Nam-ki]] presses [[Japan]] to take steps to lift its export restrictions. [https://en.yna.co.kr/view/AEN20191120006000320 (Yonhap)]
*[[2019 Hong Kong protests]]
**[[Joshua Wong]] calls on [[HSBC]] to re-open an account used to support the [[pro-democracy]] movement in the city. [https://www.telegraph.co.uk/business/2019/11/20/hong-kong-protest-leader-urges-hsbc-reopen-account-linked-pro/ (''The Telegraph'')]
*[[Google]] announces it will ban [[Targeted advertising|targeted ads]] that use voter data, effective within a week. [https://www.reuters.com/article/us-alphabet-google-advertising/google-bars-elections-ads-from-using-political-leanings-voter-data-idUSKBN1XU2WT (Reuters)]

;International relations
*[[Iran–Saudi Arabia relations]]
**[[King of Saudi Arabia|King]] [[Salman of Saudi Arabia|Salman]] of [[Saudi Arabia]] blames [[Iran]] for the "chaos and destruction" their multiple missiles and drone attacks have caused in the country, and reiterates that his country will not hesitate to defend itself. [https://www.reuters.com/article/us-saudi-king/saudi-king-blames-iran-for-chaos-says-strikes-failed-to-hurt-kingdoms-development-idUSKBN1XU1J5 (Reuters)]
*[[Pope Francis]] arrives in [[Bangkok]] for a three-day visit to [[Thailand]]. The [[Catholic Church in Thailand]] is celebrating 350 years of Holy See recognition of the Church in Thailand. Bishop [[Francis Xavier Vira Arpondratana|Arpondratana]] of [[Roman Catholic Diocese of Chiang Mai|Chiang Mai]] [[diocese]] states that the pope's visit is important for the [[Christianity in Asia|Church]] in all of Asia. [https://www.catholicnewsagency.com/news/thai-bishop-popes-visit-a-significant-moment-for-small-catholic-community-79770 (Catholic News Agency)]

;Law and crime
*[[Tonga]]n authorities contact their [[New Zealand]] counterparts to warn them of [[death threats]] against [[Tongan Prime Minister]] [[Pohiva Tuʻiʻonetoa]] on [[social media]]. [https://www.rnz.co.nz/international/pacific-news/403737/nz-police-called-in-after-death-threat-to-tongan-pm (RNZ)]
*Ali al-Haj, secretary of the [[Islamism|Islamist]] [[Popular Congress Party (Sudan)|Popular Congress Party]], is arrested after [[Sudan|Sudanese]] authorities summon him for questioning over his role in [[1989 Sudanese coup d'état|the coup d’état]] that put former President [[Omar al-Bashir]] in power. [https://www.reuters.com/article/us-sudan-politics/sudans-top-islamist-politician-sent-to-prison-holding-bashir-idUSKBN1XU292?il=0 (Reuters)]
*[[International reactions to the 2016–17 Rohingya persecution in Myanmar|International reactions to the Rohingya genocide]]
**The office of [[Myanmar]]'s [[State Counsellor of Myanmar|civilian leader]], [[Aung San Suu Kyi]], releases a statement announcing that she will personally lead the legal team defending the [[Tatmadaw|Burmese military]]'s actions against the [[Rohingya people|Rohingya minority]] in the [[International Criminal Court]]. Nine days earlier, fifty-seven countries led by [[The Gambia]] filed a lawsuit in the International Criminal Court, formally accusing Myanmar of committing [[genocide]] against the Rohingya. [https://www.cnn.com/2019/11/20/asia/aung-san-suu-kyi-rohingya-icj-intl/index.html (CNN)] [https://time.com/5735203/myanmar-suu-kyi-genocide-rohingya-icj/ (''TIME'')]

;Politics and elections
*[[2019 referendum on the creation of a Sidama region]]
**The [[Sidama people]] of [[Ethiopia]] go to the polls for a [[referendum]] on further [[autonomy]] for the [[Sidama Zone]]. If autonomy is approved, then local taxes, education, security and laws will be decided by the Sidama instead of the [[government of Ethiopia]]. [https://reuters.com/article/uk-ethiopia-politics/ethiopias-sidama-vote-on-autonomy-in-latest-test-for-restive-regions-idUKKBN1XU020 (Reuters)]
*[[2020 Israeli legislative election]]
**[[Blue and White (political alliance)|Blue and White Alliance]] leader [[Benny Gantz]]'s mandate to form a [[Thirty-fifth government of Israel|new government]] expires. As both he and [[Prime Minister of Israel|Prime Minister]] [[Benjamin Netanyahu]] failed to form one, [[Israel]] will likely face a third election in two years. [https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2019/11/israel-election-looms-deadline-form-govt-expire-191120145722129.html (Al Jazeera)]
